title: Smoked Duck Tagine
description: A traditional Moroccan stew made with tender smoked duck, aromatic spices, and a blend of sweet and tangy flavors.

ingredients.name: Smoked duck
ingredients.notes: You can use any type of smoked duck you like

ingredients.name: Rice
ingredients.notes: Uncooked white or brown rice is fine

ingredients.name: Lovely saudi saffron
ingredients.notes: Saffron adds a beautiful yellow color and a subtle earthy flavor

ingredients.name: Arabian ginger
ingredients.notes: You can also use fresh ginger

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: You can use any type of onion you like

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: You can use more or less garlic to taste

ingredients.name: Cumin
ingredients.notes: Ground cumin adds a warm, earthy flavor

ingredients.name: Paprika
ingredients.notes: Smoked paprika adds a deep, smoky flavor

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use kosher salt or sea salt for the best flavor

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use freshly ground black pepper for the best flavor

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.notes: You can use any type of oil you like

instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the duck and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper, and stir to combine.
Add the rice and stir to combine.
Add the stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Stir in the saffron and cook for 1 minute.
Serve the duck and rice hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
Cook's note: Traditionally, a tagine is cooked in a clay pot over low heat for 1-2 hours. If you have a clay pot, feel free to use it.
Nutrition information: This recipe makes 4 servings and has approximately 500 calories, 30g protein, 60g carbs, and 20g fat per serving.
